headline_marked: Dhaka outraged as [[India allows Sheikh Hasina media interaction]] in New Delhi
headline: Dhaka outraged as India allows Sheikh Hasina media interaction in New Delhi
summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs calls the event 'detrimental' to resetting bilateral ties, labeling the ousted leader as a 'convicted genocider'.
details: The Government of Bangladesh has expressed deep outrage after India allowed ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to interact with the media in New Delhi. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs described the event as 'deeply hurtful' and detrimental to the development of harmonious ties between the two nations.

In a strong statement, the ministry labeled Hasina as an 'absconding convicted genocider' and accused her and her associates of launching 'venomous vitriol' against the State of Bangladesh and its people during the interaction.
Dhaka stated that the event occurred on the second anniversary of the July Revolution, calling it an 'affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh' and a 'grievous insult' to the martyrs of the uprising.

The foreign ministry noted that it had conveyed concerns to the Indian government beforehand regarding the likely ramifications of the event on bilateral relations, but the public interaction was still permitted.

Bangladesh also accused Hasina of denying UN findings regarding the killing of civilians, including children, during the July-August 2024 uprising, asserting that the people of Bangladesh have rejected such attempts.
The government emphasized that Bangladesh will never again be a 'client state' and that Hasina and her 'mafia enterprise' will have no place in the country's future polity.
Dhaka reiterated its desire for constructive, mutually beneficial ties with New Delhi based on sovereign equality, mutual respect, and non-interference in internal affairs.
The statement also expressed regret that India has yet to respond to repeated requests for Hasina's return under the 2013 Bangladesh-India Extradition Treaty.

headline_marked: Jagannath University [[bans all rallies and gatherings]] on campus
headline: Jagannath University bans all rallies and gatherings on campus
summary: The administration prohibited all public meetings and processions until further notice to prevent law and order deterioration following recent student clashes.
details: Jagannath University (JnU) has banned all rallies, processions, and public gatherings inside the campus. The decision was made to prevent a possible deterioration of law and order on campus.
The ban follows the announcement of separate programmes by three different organisations scheduled for the same venue and time on August 6.

These organisations included the Jagannath University Central Students' Union (Jnucsu), which planned to donate an ambulance, and Chhatra Dal, which planned a protest against alleged criminal activities by Islamic Chhatra Shibir.
Additionally, a group of general students had announced a protest procession regarding an alleged attack on university students by Suhrawardy College Chhatra Dal activists.
The move comes after clashes broke out on August 4 between activists of Chhatra Dal, Shibir, and other student organisations during July Uprising Day programmes.
Several students, including JnUCSU leaders, were injured during those clashes, prompting the university administration to strengthen security measures.
The administration had already announced additional security arrangements for August 5 and 6, which has now evolved into a total ban on political programmes until further notice.
caption:
Three different student groups planned protests at the same time and place—now all gatherings are banned at Jagannath University.

Jagannath University (JnU) has banned all rallies, processions, and public gatherings inside the campus. The decision was made to prevent a possible deterioration of law and order on campus.

The ban follows the announcement of separate programmes by three different organisations scheduled for the same venue and time on August 6.

These organisations included the Jagannath University Central Students' Union (Jnucsu), which planned to donate an ambulance, and Chhatra Dal, which planned a protest against alleged criminal activities by Islamic Chhatra Shibir.

Additionally, a group of general students had announced a protest procession regarding an alleged attack on university students by Suhrawardy College Chhatra Dal activists.

The move comes after clashes broke out on August 4 between activists of Chhatra Dal, Shibir, and other student organisations during July Uprising Day programmes.

Several students, including JnUCSU leaders, were injured during those clashes, prompting the university administration to strengthen security measures.

The administration had already announced additional security arrangements for August 5 and 6, which has now evolved into a total ban on political programmes until further notice.
